curiosities: Acorn built it for the BBC's Computer Literacy Project, and it became a fixture of British classrooms.
Elite was first released on it in 1984.
Its designers Sophie Wilson and Steve Furber later created the ARM processor.
The 1986 BBC Domesday Project put a survey of the UK on LaserVision discs read by a BBC Master.
Its processor is a 6502 at 2 MHz.
The Model A has 16 KB of memory and the Model B 32 KB.
BBC BASIC can include assembly language in a program.
Its Mode 7 shows teletext graphics, using little memory.
The BBC Master of 1986 was its successor.
